How much does flooring installation cost?

New floors through a room or the whole house — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$1,528–$4,850
500 sq ft installed, national — average about $3,153

National average $3,153 per 500 sq ft · about $12.50 per sq ft

Bay Area: $2,500–$6,800 per 500 sq ft — about $16.50 per sq ft, with labor alone at $4–$10 per sq ft.

What drives the price

Why quotes run $3 to $25 per sq ft

Four things move the price:

Material
The whole game: vinyl $2–$14 per sq ft, laminate $3–$13, engineered wood $4.50–$16, hardwood $6–$25, tile $15–$20.
Room size
Per-square-foot pricing means size is destiny — but small jobs can carry a higher rate so the crew meets its minimum.
Old floor removal
Tearing out the old floor costs $1.50–$3.50 per sq ft — tile removal alone runs $2–$7. DIY removal saves real money if the subfloor survives.
Subfloor & extras
Subfloor replacement runs $3–$10 per sq ft; underlayment adds $0.50–$5.40. Stairs cost $11–$160 per step.
Material

Synthetic or the real thing

Laminate / vinyl
$2–$14 per sq ft

The budget play that looks like wood. Fast to install, easy to clean, lasts 10–30 years. Can't be refinished — when it's done, it's done.

Hardwood
$6–$25 per sq ft

The real thing: can be refinished, lasts 30–100 years, and returns 70–80% at resale in San Francisco. Costs two to three times the synthetics.

Bottom line: vinyl or laminate for rentals and busy households; hardwood where you'll stay a decade and want the resale bump.

Questions

Common questions

How long does flooring installation take?

A 200-sq-ft laminate room can wrap in about three hours. Tile takes a full day with layout and curing. Whole houses take several days.

Should I refinish or replace hardwood?

Refinish when the wood is solid but tired — about $3–$8 per sq ft. Replace when boards are warped, deeply gouged, or the subfloor is shot.

Can I install flooring myself?

Laminate and vinyl plank are realistic DIY. Hardwood and tile punish mistakes — uneven subfloors and bad cuts show forever.

Does new flooring add home value?

Hardwood does — about 75% ROI nationally, 70–80% in San Francisco. Even new carpet or vinyl lifts a listing, just for less.

Every home prices differently.

The range above is a national average. Your price depends on the material, square footage, and local labor rates. Take a photo of your floors in Brightglow for an estimate on the actual space, and to compare local pros who've done the same work.
